text:
A student performed analysis of aliphatic organic compound ‘X’ which on analysis gave C = 61.01%, H = 15.25%, N = 23.74%.
This compound, on treatment with HNO$_{2}/H_{2}O$ produced another compound ‘Y’ which did not contain any nitrogen atom. However, the compound ‘Y’ upon controlled oxidation produced another compound ‘Z’ that responded to iodoform test.
The structure of ‘X’ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Mole ratio from the analysis: C, $61.01/12=5.08$; H, $15.25/1=15.25$; N, $23.74/14=1.70$. Dividing by 1.70 gives C : H : N = 3 : 9 : 1, so X is $\mathrm{C}{}_{3}\mathrm{H}{}_{9}\mathrm{N}$ (M = 59; C = 36/59 = 61.0%).

Only (B) and (D) are $\mathrm{C}{}_{3}\mathrm{H}{}_{9}\mathrm{N}$; (A) is $\mathrm{C}{}_{4}\mathrm{H}{}_{11}\mathrm{N}$ (C = 65.8%) and (C) is the aromatic $\mathrm{C}{}_{8}\mathrm{H}{}_{11}\mathrm{N}$.

X is a primary aliphatic amine: $\mathrm{HNO}{}_{2}$ converts it, with loss of $\mathrm{N}{}_{2}$, into an alcohol Y that contains no nitrogen.

For (D), isopropylamine gives propan-2-ol, $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{CHOH}$, whose controlled oxidation gives acetone Z, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COCH}{}_{3}$, a methyl ketone that gives the iodoform test.


[IMG]

For (B), propan-1-amine gives propan-1-ol, which is oxidised to propanal, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CHO}$; it has no $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CO}{}^{-}$ group and gives no iodoform test.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text:
Match List - I with List - II according to shape.

  

    List – I

    List – II

  

  

    

      A.  XeO$_{3}$

      B.  XeF$_{2}$

      C.  XeO$_{2}F_{2}$

      D.  XeOF$_{4}$

    

    

      I.  BrF$_{5}$

      $II.  NH_{3}$

      III.  [$I_{3}$]$^{−}$

      $IV.  SF_{4}$

    

  

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The shape follows from the numbers of bond pairs (bp) and lone pairs (lp) on the central atom.

A. $\mathrm{XeO}{}_{3}$ has 3 bp + 1 lp, so it is trigonal pyramidal, like $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ (II).

B. $\mathrm{XeF}{}_{2}$ has 2 bp + 3 lp, so it is linear, like $\mathrm{I}{}_{3}{}^{-}$ (III).

C. $\mathrm{XeO}{}_{2}\mathrm{F}{}_{2}$ has 4 bp + 1 lp, so it is see-saw, like $\mathrm{SF}{}_{4}$ (IV).

D. $\mathrm{XeOF}{}_{4}$ has 5 bp + 1 lp, so it is square pyramidal, like $\mathrm{BrF}{}_{5}$ (I).

The match is A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

text:
Consider the following reactions
$\mathrm{Na}_{2}\mathrm{B}_{4}\mathrm{O}_{7}\leftarrow ^{\Delta }2X+Y$
$\mathrm{CuSO}_{4}+Y\leftarrow ^{\text{Non-Luminous flame}}Z+SO_{3}$
$2Z+2X+\text{Carbon}\leftarrow ^{\text{Luminous flame}}2Q+\mathrm{Na}_{2}\mathrm{B}_{4}\mathrm{O}_{7}+CO$
The oxidation states of Cu in Z and Q, respectively are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
On heating, borax gives sodium metaborate and boric anhydride, so X is $\mathrm{NaBO}{}_{2}$ and Y is $\mathrm{B}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{3}$:

$\mathrm{Na}{}_{2}\mathrm{B}{}_{4}\mathrm{O}{}_{7}{}^{\Delta }2\mathrm{NaBO}{}_{2}+\mathrm{B}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{3}$

In the non-luminous (oxidising) flame, $\mathrm{CuSO}{}_{4}$ forms blue copper(II) metaborate, Z:

$\mathrm{CuSO}{}_{4}+\mathrm{B}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{3}\longrightarrow \mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{BO}{}_{2}){}_{2}+\mathrm{SO}{}_{3}$

In $\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{BO}{}_{2}){}_{2}$, each $\mathrm{BO}{}_{2}{}^{-}$ carries $-1$, so Cu is $+2$.

In the luminous (reducing) flame, carbon reduces Z to colourless copper(I) metaborate, Q:

$2~\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{BO}{}_{2}){}_{2}+2\mathrm{NaBO}{}_{2}+\mathrm{C}\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{CuBO}{}_{2}+\mathrm{Na}{}_{2}\mathrm{B}{}_{4}\mathrm{O}{}_{7}+\mathrm{CO}$

In $\mathrm{CuBO}{}_{2}$, Cu is $+1$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : The increasing order of boiling point of hydrogen halides is HCl Statement II : The increasing order of melting point of hydrogen halides is HCl correct answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Correct order of

(i) Boiling point: $\mathrm{HF}>\mathrm{HI}>\mathrm{HBr}>\mathrm{HCl}$

As we go from $\mathrm{HCl}$ to $\mathrm{HI}$, the size and molar mass increase, so van der Waals forces increase and the boiling point increases.

But $\mathrm{HF}$ has strong hydrogen bonding because fluorine is highly electronegative, so its boiling point becomes the highest.

(ii) Melting point : $\mathrm{HI}>\mathrm{HF}>\mathrm{HBr}>\mathrm{HCl}$

In general, from $\mathrm{HCl}$ to $\mathrm{HI}$, increasing size and mass increase intermolecular forces, so melting point increases.

However, $\mathrm{HF}$ shows hydrogen bonding, so its melting point is higher than $\mathrm{HCl}$ and $\mathrm{HBr}$.

Overall, $\mathrm{HI}$ has the highest melting point among hydrogen halides due to stronger dispersion forces in the solid state.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

text:
Consider the following statements about manganate and permanganate ions. Identify the correct statements.
A. The geometry of both manganate and permanganate ions is tetrahedral.
B. The oxidation states of Mn in manganate and permanganate are +7 and +6, respectively.
C. Oxidation of Mn(II) salt by peroxodisulphate gives manganate ion as the final product.
D. Manganate ion is paramagnetic and permanganate ion is diamagnetic.
E. Acidified permanganate ion reduces oxalate, nitrite and iodide ions.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Manganate is $\mathrm{MnO}{}_{4}{}^{2-}$ (Mn in $+6$ state, $3d^{1}$) and permanganate is $\mathrm{MnO}{}_{4}{}^{-}$ (Mn in $+7$ state, $3d^{0}$).

A: In both ions Mn is surrounded tetrahedrally by four O atoms, so both are tetrahedral: true.

B: $x-8=-2$ gives $+6$ for manganate and $x-8=-1$ gives $+7$ for permanganate; the statement reverses them: false.

C: Peroxodisulphate oxidises $\mathrm{Mn}{}^{2+}$ all the way to permanganate: $2~\mathrm{Mn}{}^{2+}+5\mathrm{S}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{8}{}^{2-}+8\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{MnO}{}_{4}{}^{-}+10\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}{}^{2-}+16\mathrm{H}{}^{+}$; false.

D: Manganate has one unpaired electron ($3d^{1}$) and is paramagnetic; permanganate has none ($3d^{0}$) and is diamagnetic: true.

E: Acidified permanganate is a strong oxidising agent; it oxidises oxalate to $\mathrm{CO}{}_{2}$, nitrite to nitrate and iodide to $\mathrm{I}{}_{2}$, and is itself reduced to $\mathrm{Mn}{}^{2+}$: false.

The correct statements are A and D only.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

text: The wavelength of photon 'A' is 400 nm. The frequency of photon 'B' is $10^{16}\text{s}^{-1}$. The wave number of photon 'C' is $10^{4}\text{cm}^{-1}$. The correct order of energy of these photons is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\text{(1) Wavelength of}\mathrm{A}=400\mathrm{nm}\text{.}$

$\text{(2) For photon}\mathrm{B},λ=\frac{\mathrm{C}}{v}=\frac{3\times 10^{8}}{10^{16}}$

$=3\times 10^{-8}\text{m}=30\times 10^{-9}\text{m}=30\mathrm{nm}.$

(3) For photon $\mathrm{C}$, wave number is given, and $\bar{v}=\frac{1}{λ}$. So $\mathrm{C}(λ)=\frac{1}{\bar{v}}=\frac{1}{10^{4}}=10^{-4}\mathrm{cm}=10^{-6}\mathrm{m}=1000\mathrm{nm}$

Now compare the wavelengths: $λ_{\mathrm{C}}>λ_{\mathrm{A}}>λ_{\mathrm{B}}$

Energy of a photon is inversely proportional to wavelength: Energy(E) $\propto \frac{1}{λ}$

So, smaller wavelength means higher energy. Therefore: $\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{B}}>\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{A}}>\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{C}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

text:
For the given reaction;
CaCO$_{3} + 2$HCl → CaCl$_{2} + H_{2}O + CO_{2}$
If 90 g CaCO$_{3}$ is added to 300 mL of HCl which contains 38.55% HCl by mass and has density $1.13 g mL^{$−1}, then which of the following option is correct?
Given molar mass of H, Cl, Ca and O are 1, 35.5, 40 and 16 g mol$^{$−1} respectively.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Mass of HCl solution $=1.13\times 300=339\text{g}$, so mass of HCl $=339\times \dfrac{38.55}{100}=130.68\text{g}$, i.e. $\dfrac{130.68}{36.5}=3.58\text{mol}$.

Moles of $\mathrm{CaCO}{}_{3}$ $=\dfrac{90}{100}=0.90\text{mol}$; by the equation it needs $2\times 0.90=1.80\text{mol}$ of $\mathrm{HCl}$ $=1.80\times 36.5=65.70\text{g}$.

Since $1.80<3.58$, $\mathrm{CaCO}{}_{3}$ is the limiting reagent: it is used up completely, and only $65.70\text{g}$ of $\mathrm{HCl}$ reacts.

$\mathrm{HCl}$ left unreacted $=3.58-1.80=1.78\text{mol}=1.78\times 36.5=64.97\text{g}$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

text: Consider the elements N, P, O, S, Cl and F. The number of valence electrons present in the elements with most and least metallic character from the above list is respectively.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Metallic character increases down a group and decreases from left to right across a period (NCERT trend).

Given elements:

Period 2: $N,O,F$

Period 3: $P,S,Cl$

1) Most metallic element
In period 3, metallic character is higher than in period 2, and within period 3 it decreases left to right:

$P>S>Cl$

So, $P$ is the most metallic among the given elements.

Valence electrons in $P$ (Group 15) $=5$.

2) Least metallic element
Least metallic means most non-metallic, which is highest towards the top-right of the periodic table. Among the given, $F$ is the most non-metallic.

Valence electrons in $F$ (Group 17) $=7$.

Final Answer
Number of valence electrons (most metallic, least metallic) $=(5,7)$.

Option C: 5 and 7

text:
Observe the following equilibrium in a 1 L flask.
 A(g) ⇌ B(g)
 At T(K), the equilibrium concentrations of A and B are 0.5 M and 0.375 M respectively. 0.1 moles of A is added into the flask and heated to T(K) to establish the equilibrium again. The new equilibrium concentrations (in M) of A and B are respectively
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
At the first equilibrium, $K_{c}=\dfrac{[\mathrm{B}]}{[\mathrm{A}]}=\dfrac{0.375}{0.5}=0.75$.

Adding 0.1 mol of A to the 1 L flask raises $[\mathrm{A}]$ to $0.5+0.1=0.6\text{M}$ while $[\mathrm{B}]$ stays $0.375\text{M}$. Then $Q=\dfrac{0.375}{0.6}=0.625<K_{c}$, so the reaction shifts forward by $x\text{M}$: $[\mathrm{A}]=0.6-x$, $[\mathrm{B}]=0.375+x$.

$0.75=\dfrac{0.375+x}{0.6-x}\Rightarrow 0.45-0.75x=0.375+x\Rightarrow 1.75x=0.075\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{3}{70}\approx 0.043$

$[\mathrm{A}]=0.6-0.043=0.557\text{M},[\mathrm{B}]=0.375+0.043=0.418\text{M}$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

The correct increasing order of spin-only magnetic moment values of the complex ions 

[MnBr$_{4}$]$^{2−} (A)$, [$Cu(H_{2}O)_{6}$]$^{2+} (B)$, [$Ni(CN)_{4}$]$^{2−} (C)$ and [$Ni(H_{2}O)_{6}$]$^{2+} (D)$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body: $\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{Mn}^{2+}:3\mathrm{d}^{5} \\ \text{In}[\mathrm{MnBr}_{4}]^{2-}\text{, Mn is in}+2\text{oxidation state, so configuration is}3d^{5}. \\ \text{Br}^{-}\text{is a weak field ligand and the complex is tetrahedral, so it is high spin.} \\ \text{Hence number of unpaired electrons}(n)=5. \\  \\ \mathrm{Cu}^{2+}:3\mathrm{d}^{9} \\ \text{In}[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{2+}\text{, Cu is in}+2\text{oxidation state, so configuration is}3d^{9}. \\ \text{This is an octahedral complex (six water ligands). In}d^{9}\text{, there is always one unpaired electron.} \\ \text{So}\mathrm{t}_{2\mathrm{g}}^{2,2,2}\mathrm{e}_{\mathrm{g}}^{2,1}\text{and}(n)=1. \\  \\ \mathrm{Ni}^{2+}:3\mathrm{d}^{8} \\ \text{In}[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}]^{2-}\text{, Ni is in}+2\text{oxidation state, so configuration is}3d^{8}. \\ \text{CN}^{-}\text{is a strong field ligand, so electrons pair up and the complex becomes square planar.} \\ \text{In square planar}d^{8}\text{, all electrons are paired, so}(n)=0. \\  \\ \mathrm{Ni}^{2+}:3\mathrm{d}^{8}\text{(octahedral)} \\ \text{In}[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{2+}\text{, Ni is in}+2\text{oxidation state, so configuration is}3d^{8}. \\ \text{With}\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}\text{(weak field), the complex is high spin; the distribution gives two unpaired electrons.} \\ \text{So}\mathrm{t}_{2g}^{2,2,2}\mathrm{e}_{g}^{1,1}\text{and}(n)=2. \end{array}$

text:
The correct order of acidic strength of the major products formed in the given reactions, is :
A. $\mathrm{PhNH}_{2}\leftarrow _{\begin{array}{l} \text{(2)}\mathrm{CuCN} \\ \text{(3)}\mathrm{H}_{3}\mathrm{O}^{+}/\Delta  \end{array}}^{\text{(1)}\mathrm{NaNO}_{2}+\mathrm{HCl}(<5^{\circ }\mathrm{C})}[\mathrm{A}]$

B. $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{CHO}\leftarrow _{\Delta }^{[\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{2}]^{+},\mathrm{OH}^{-}}[\mathrm{B}]$

C. $\mathrm{CH}_{4}+\mathrm{O}_{2}\leftarrow _{\text{(ii)}\mathrm{Na}_{2}\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}/\mathrm{H}^{+}}^{\text{(i)}\mathrm{Mo}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}}[\mathrm{C}]$

D. $\mathrm{PhCH}_{2}\mathrm{MgBr}+\mathrm{CO}_{2}\leftarrow _{\mathrm{H}_{3}\mathrm{O}^{+}}^{\text{Dry ether}}[\mathrm{D}]$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(A) Aniline is diazotised, CuCN converts the diazonium salt to benzonitrile and acid hydrolysis gives benzoic acid: $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}{}^{\mathrm{NaNO}{}_{2}/\mathrm{HCl}}\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{N}{}_{2}{}^{+}\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}{}^{\mathrm{CuCN}\qquad }\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{CN}{}^{\mathrm{H}{}_{3}\mathrm{O}{}^{+}}\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{COOH}$.

(B) Tollens' reagent oxidises propanal to propanoic acid, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{COOH}$.

(C) Methane and $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$ over $\mathrm{Mo}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{3}$ give methanal, which acidified dichromate oxidises to methanoic acid, $\mathrm{HCOOH}$.

(D) Benzylmagnesium bromide with $\mathrm{CO}{}_{2}$ followed by $\mathrm{H}{}_{3}\mathrm{O}{}^{+}$ gives phenylacetic acid, $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{COOH}$.

$\mathrm{HCOOH}$ ($\mathrm{p}K_{\mathrm{a}}$ 3.75) carries no electron-donating group and is the strongest. In benzoic acid ($\mathrm{p}K_{\mathrm{a}}$ 4.20) the $\mathrm{sp}^{2}$ ring carbon attached to $\mathrm{COOH}$ withdraws electrons. In phenylacetic acid ($\mathrm{p}K_{\mathrm{a}}$ 4.31) the $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ leaves only a weak $-I$ effect of phenyl, which still makes it stronger than propanoic acid ($\mathrm{p}K_{\mathrm{a}}$ 4.87) with its $+I$ ethyl group.

So the order of acidic strength is C > A > D > B.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

text:
Consider the following aqueous solutions.

I. 2.2 g Glucose in 125 mL of solution.

II. 1.9 g Calcium chloride in 250 mL of solution.

III. 9.0 g Urea in 500 mL of solution.

IV. 20.5 g Aluminium sulphate in 750 mL of solution.

The correct increasing order of boiling point of these solutions will be :

[Given : Molar mass in g mol$^{−1}$ : H = 1, C = 12, N = 14, O = 16, Cl = 35.5, Ca = 40, Al = 27 and S = 32]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For aqueous solutions $\Delta T_{b}=iK_{b}m$, and with the same solvent and dilute solutions ($m\approx M$) the boiling point rises with $i\times M$.

I. Glucose (molar mass 180, $i=1$): $M=\dfrac{2.2}{180}\times \dfrac{1000}{125}=0.098$, so $iM=0.098$.

II. $\mathrm{CaCl}{}_{2}$ (molar mass $40+71=111$, $i=3$): $M=\dfrac{1.9}{111}\times \dfrac{1000}{250}=0.068$, so $iM=0.205$.

III. Urea, $\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CONH}{}_{2}$ (molar mass 60, $i=1$): $M=\dfrac{9.0}{60}\times \dfrac{1000}{500}=0.30$, so $iM=0.30$.

IV. $\mathrm{Al}{}_{2}(\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}){}_{3}$ (molar mass $2(27)+3(96)=342$, $i=5$): $M=\dfrac{20.5}{342}\times \dfrac{1000}{750}=0.080$, so $iM=0.40$.

Increasing $iM$, and hence increasing boiling point: I < II < III < IV.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

text: A student has been given 0.314 g of an organic compound and asked to estimate Sulphur. During the experiment, the student has obtained 0.4813 g of barium sulphate. The percentage of sulphur present in the compound is $_________. ($Given Molar mass in g mol$^{−1} S$: 32, BaSO$_{4}$: 233)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Mass of compound taken $=0.314\text{g}$

Mass of $BaSO_{4}$ obtained $=0.4813\text{g}$

In $BaSO_{4}$, sulphur present per mole $=32\text{g}$  

Molar mass of $BaSO_{4}=233\text{g mol}^{-1}$

So, mass of sulphur in $0.4813\text{g}$ of $BaSO_{4}$ is:

$m(S)=0.4813\times \frac{32}{233}$

$m(S)=0.4813\times \frac{32}{233}=0.06608\text{g (approx.)}$

Percentage of sulphur in the compound:

$%S=\frac{0.06608}{0.314}\times 100\approx 21.05%$

Correct option: B) $21.05%$

text: Which of the following reactions is NOT correctly represented?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Bromination with $\mathrm{Br}{}_{2}/hν$ is a free-radical substitution that takes place where the most stable radical forms.

In (A) the substrate is 3-methylcyclohexene: its ring C–H at C-3 is both tertiary and allylic, so the radical forms there and bromine enters the ring (3-bromo-3-methylcyclohexene), not the methyl group; the primary bromide shown is not the major product.

In (C) toluene has only benzylic C–H in the side chain, so $\mathrm{Br}{}_{2}/hν$ correctly gives benzyl bromide; (B) is the Sandmeyer reaction giving bromobenzene, and (D) is ring bromination with $\mathrm{Br}{}_{2}$/Fe in the dark giving o- and p-bromotoluene.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
Identify the correct statements :
The presence of –$NO_{2}$ group in benzene ring
A. activates the ring towards electrophilic substitutions.
B. deactivates the ring towards electrophilic substitutions.
C. activates the ring towards nucleophilic substitutions.
D. deactivates the ring towards nucleophilic substitutions.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Presence of $\mathrm{NO}_{2}$ group on the benzene ring deactivates the ring towards electrophilic substitution reactions because it shows $-M$ effect (it withdraws electrons from the ring by resonance).

Because the $\mathrm{NO}_{2}$ group pulls electron density away, the ring becomes less reactive towards electrophiles.

At the same time, the $\mathrm{NO}_{2}$ group activates the ring towards nucleophilic substitution because the withdrawal of electrons makes the ring more suitable for attack by nucleophiles (electron-rich species).

Ans. $\to$ B & C
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

text: The number of isoelectronic species among $Sc^{3+},Cr^{2+},Mn^{3+},Co^{3+}$ and $Fe^{3+}$ is ‘n’. If ‘n’ moles of AgCl is formed during the reaction of complex with formula $CoCl_{3}(en)_{2}NH_{3}$ with excess of $AgNO_{3}$ solution, then the number of electrons present in the $t_{2g}$ orbital of the complex is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{ll} \mathrm{Sc}^{+3} & 18 \\ \mathrm{Cr}^{+2} & 22 \\ \mathrm{Mn}^{+3} & 22 \\ \mathrm{Co}^{+3} & 24 \\ \mathrm{Fe}^{+3} & 23 \end{array}$

In the table, the number written for each ion is its total number of electrons.

$\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}$ both have $22$ electrons, so they are isoelectronic (same number of electrons).

So, the number of isoelectronic species is

$\mathrm{n}=2$

Now, for the complex $CoCl_{3}(en)_{2}NH_{3}$:

$en$ and $NH_{3}$ are neutral ligands, so they do not change the charge.

In the given formula, total $Cl$ are $3$. If $n=2$ moles of $AgCl$ are formed with excess $AgNO_{3}$, it means $2$ chloride ions are outside the coordination sphere (they are ionisable and precipitate as $AgCl$).

So the complex must be:

Complex is : $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_{2}\mathrm{NH}_{3}\mathrm{Cl}]\mathrm{Cl}_{2}$

Here, $2$ $Cl^{-}$ are outside, so the complex ion has charge $+2$.

Let oxidation state of Co be $x$.

Inside the bracket: $en$ and $NH_{3}$ contribute $0$, and one coordinated $Cl^{-}$ contributes $-1$.

So, $x-1=+2\Rightarrow x=+3$.

Thus cobalt is $Co^{3+}$, and its $d$-electron configuration is:

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{Co}^{3+}3\mathrm{d}^{6}\mathrm{t}_{2\mathrm{g}}^{2,2,2}\mathrm{e}_{\mathrm{g}}^{0,0}$

So, total electrons in $t_{2g}$ orbitals $=2+2+2=6$.

text:
A volume of x mL of 5 M NaHCO$_{3}$ solution was mixed with 10 mL of $2 M H_{2}CO_{3}$ solution to make an electrolytic buffer. If the same buffer was used in the following electrochemical cell to record a cell potential of 235.3 mV, then the value of $x = ______ mL ($nearest integer).
 $Sn(s) | Sn(OH)_{6}^{2−} (0.5 M) |$ HSnO$_{2}^{−} (0.05 M) | OH^{−} | Bi_{2}O_{3}(s) | Bi(s)$
 Consider up to one place of decimal for intermediate calculations
 
$\left [\begin{array}{ll} \text{Given:} & E_{Sn(OH)_{6}^{2-}|HSnO_{2}^{-}}^{o}=-0.9V \\  & \mathrm{E}^{\mathrm{o}}{}_{\mathrm{Bi}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}|\mathrm{Bi}}=-0.44\mathrm{V} \\  & \mathrm{pKa}_{(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{CO}_{3})}=6.11 \\  & \frac{2.303\mathrm{RT}}{\mathrm{F}}=0.059\mathrm{V} \\  & \text{Antilog}(1.29)=19.5 \end{array}\right ]$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For the half-cells (25 °C):

(1) Sn(IV)/Sn(II) couple (given $E^{\circ }=-0.90\text{V}$)  

Balanced reduction in basic medium:

$\mathrm{Sn}(\mathrm{OH})_{6}^{2-}+2\mathrm{e}^{-}\to \mathrm{HSnO}_{2}^{-}+3\mathrm{OH}^{-}+\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

$E_{\text{Sn}}=E_{\text{Sn}}^{\circ }-\frac{0.059}{2}\log \left (\frac{[HSnO_{2}^{-}][OH^{-}]^{3}}{[Sn(OH)_{6}^{2-}]}\right )$

Given $[Sn(OH)_{6}^{2-}]=0.5$, $[HSnO_{2}^{-}]=0.05$:

$\frac{[HSnO_{2}^{-}]}{[Sn(OH)_{6}^{2-}]}=\frac{0.05}{0.5}=0.1$

(2) Bi${}_{2}$O${}_{3}$/Bi couple (given $E^{\circ }=-0.44\text{V}$)  

Reduction:

$\mathrm{Bi}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}(\mathrm{s})+3\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}+6\mathrm{e}^{-}\to 2\mathrm{Bi}(\mathrm{s})+6\mathrm{OH}^{-}$

$E_{\text{Bi}}=E_{\text{Bi}}^{\circ }-\frac{0.059}{6}\log ([OH^{-}]^{6})=E_{\text{Bi}}^{\circ }-0.059\log [OH^{-}]$

Bi has higher $E^{\circ }$, so it is the cathode. Thus

$E_{\text{cell}}=E_{\text{cathode}}-E_{\text{anode}}=E_{\text{Bi}}-E_{\text{Sn}}$

Substitute and simplify:

$E_{\text{cell}}=(-0.44-0.059\log [OH^{-}])-\left (-0.90-\frac{0.059}{2}\log (0.1[OH^{-}]^{3})\right )$

$E_{\text{cell}}=0.46-0.059\log [OH^{-}]+\frac{0.059}{2}(\log 0.1+3\log [OH^{-}])$

Since $\log 0.1=-1$:

$E_{\text{cell}}=0.46+\frac{0.059}{2}(-1)+\left (-0.059+\frac{3\cdot 0.059}{2}\right )\log [OH^{-}]$

$E_{\text{cell}}=0.4305+0.0295\log [OH^{-}]$

Given $E_{\text{cell}}=0.2353\text{V}$:

$0.2353=0.4305+0.0295\log [OH^{-}]\Rightarrow \log [OH^{-}]=\frac{-0.1952}{0.0295}\approx -6.6$

So $pOH\approx 6.6\Rightarrow pH\approx 14-6.6=7.4$.

Buffer calculation (H${}_{2}$CO${}_{3}$/HCO${}_{3}^{-}$)
Henderson–Hasselbalch:

$pH=pK_{a}+\log \frac{[HCO_{3}^{-}]}{[H_{2}CO_{3}]}$

$7.4=6.11+\log \frac{[HCO_{3}^{-}]}{[H_{2}CO_{3}]}\Rightarrow \log \frac{[HCO_{3}^{-}]}{[H_{2}CO_{3}]}=1.29\Rightarrow \frac{[HCO_{3}^{-}]}{[H_{2}CO_{3}]}=19.5$

Moles mixed:

$n(H_{2}CO_{3})=2\text{M}\times 10\text{mL}=2\times 0.010=0.020\text{mol}$

$n(HCO_{3}^{-})=5\text{M}\times x\text{mL}=5\times \frac{x}{1000}=0.005x\text{mol}$

Ratio $=19.5$:

$\frac{0.005x}{0.020}=19.5\Rightarrow 0.005x=0.39\Rightarrow x=78$

Answer: $78\text{mL}$

text:
For strong electrolyte $\Lambda _{m}$ increases slowly with dilution and can be represented by the equation
$\Lambda _{m}=\Lambda _{m}^{\circ }-Ac^{1/2}$
Molar conductivity values of the solutions of strong electrolyte AB at 18°C are given below :
c [mol $L^{-1}$]0.040.090.160.25$\Lambda _{m}$ [$S cm^{2}$ mol$^{-1}$]96.195.795.394.9The value of constant A based on the above data [in $S cm^{2}$ mol$^{-1}/($mol$/L)^{1/2}$] unit is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We use the given relation for a strong electrolyte:

Using equation : $\Lambda _{\mathrm{m}}=\Lambda _{\mathrm{m}}^{0}-\mathrm{A}\sqrt{\mathrm{c}}$

Now substitute the first set of data: $c=0.04$ and $\Lambda _{m}=96.1$.

$\begin{array}{l} 96.1=\Lambda _{\mathrm{m}}^{0}-\mathrm{A}\sqrt{0.04} \\ 96.1=\Lambda _{\mathrm{m}}^{0}-\mathrm{A}\times 0.2...(i) \\ 95.7=\Lambda _{\mathrm{m}}^{0}-\mathrm{A}\times \sqrt{0.09} \\ 95.7=\Lambda _{\mathrm{m}}^{0}-\mathrm{A}\times 0.3...(ii) \end{array}$

Now subtract equation (ii) from equation (i) so that $\Lambda _{\mathrm{m}}^{0}$ cancels out:

From eq. (1) and eq. (2)

$\begin{array}{ll} (96.1-95.7) & =(\Lambda _{\mathrm{m}}^{0}-A\times 0.2)-(\Lambda _{\mathrm{m}}^{0}-A\times 0.3) \\ 0.4 & =-0.2A+0.3A \\ 0.4 & =0.1A \\ A & =4 \end{array}$

text:
Two positively charged particles $m_{1}$ and $m_{2}$ have been accelerated across the same potential difference of 200 keV as shown below.

[IMG]
[Given mass of $m_{1}=1$ amu and $m_{2}=4$ amu]

The deBroglie wavelength of $m_{1}$ will be $x$ times of $m_{2}$. The value of $x$ is $__________ ($nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$λ_{\mathrm{d}}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\sqrt{2\mathrm{mK}.\mathrm{E}.}}$

Here, both particles are accelerated through the same potential difference of 200 keV, so they gain the same kinetic energy (K.E.).

So, in the formula, $\mathrm{h}$ and K.E. are the same for both particles. Only the mass $\mathrm{m}$ is different.

Therefore, $λ_{\mathrm{d}}\propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mathrm{m}}}$

Now, $\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{(λ_{\mathrm{d}})_{\mathrm{m}_{1}}}{(λ_{\mathrm{d}})_{\mathrm{m}_{2}}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{\mathrm{m}_{2}}{\mathrm{m}_{1}}}=\sqrt{4}=2 \\ (λ_{\mathrm{d}})_{\mathrm{m}_{1}}=2(λ_{\mathrm{d}})_{\mathrm{m}_{2}} \end{array}$

So $\mathrm{x}=2$.

C → D (second reaction)
Consider the above two first-order reactions. The rate constant for first reaction at 500 K is double of the same at 300 K. At 500 K, 50% of the reaction becomes complete in 2 hour. The activation energy of the second reaction is half of that of first reaction. If the rate constant at 500 K of the second reaction becomes double of the rate constant of first reaction at the same temperature; then rate constant for the second reaction at 300 K is $_______$ × $10^{-1}$ hour$^{-1} ($nearest integer).
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\text{For}\mathrm{A}\leftarrow ^{\mathrm{K}_{1}}\mathrm{B}$

$\begin{array}{l} \ln (2)=\dfrac{E_{a_{1}}}{R}\left [\dfrac{1}{300}-\dfrac{1}{500}\right ] \\ E_{a_{1}}=\dfrac{\ln 2\times R\times 1500}{2} \\ E_{a_{2}}=\dfrac{E_{a_{1}}}{2}=\dfrac{\ln 2\times R\times 1500}{4} \\ (K_{1})_{\text{at}500\mathrm{K}}=\dfrac{\ln 2}{2} \\ (K_{2})_{\text{at}500\mathrm{K}}=\ln 2 \end{array}$

Now for $\mathrm{C}\leftarrow ^{\mathrm{K}_{2}}\mathrm{D}$

$\begin{array}{l} \ln \left [\dfrac{(\mathrm{K}_{2})_{\text{at}500\mathrm{K}}}{(\mathrm{K}_{2})_{\text{at}300\mathrm{K}}}\right ]=\left (\dfrac{\ln 2\times \mathrm{R}\times 1500}{4}\right )\times \dfrac{1}{\mathrm{R}}\times \left [\dfrac{1}{300}-\dfrac{1}{500}\right ] \\ (\mathrm{K}_{2})_{\text{at}300\mathrm{K}}=\dfrac{\ln 2}{\sqrt{2}}=0.49 \\ (\mathrm{K}_{2})_{\text{at}300\mathrm{K}}=4.9\times 10^{-1} \end{array}$

Ans is 5 .
